info.name: RunCloud API v3
info.description:
RunCloud v3 REST API.

## Setup

1. Import the companion environment file, or set collection variables directly.
2. Put your key in `apiToken` (Workspace > Settings > API Key).
3. Run **00 · Connectivity > Ping** — it should return `{"message":"pong"}`.

Auth is inherited by every request from the collection, so no request carries the token itself.

## Conventions

- **Envelope is inconsistent.** List endpoints return `{data:[...], meta:{pagination:{...}}}`. Single-resource, delete, and services endpoints return bare objects. Do not write one generic unwrapper.
- **Pagination** is `page` and `perPage`, capped at 40 — except web apps and domains, which cap at 20.
- **Rate limits** surface as `X-RateLimit-Limit` / `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and 429 when exceeded.
- **403 usually means scope, not syntax.** RunCloud scopes API keys per resource type, so a key that lists servers happily can still be refused on Git.

## Secrets in responses

Web app responses embed `pullKey1`/`pullKey2` — Git deploy keys. Postman syncs collections and history to the cloud by default, so be deliberate about saving those responses as examples.

exec: // Surface rate-limit headroom and the common failure modes.
console.warn('RunCloud rate limit nearly exhausted: ' + remaining + ' remaining');
console.error('403 — the API key lacks permission for this resource. RunCloud scopes keys per resource type; check Workspace > Settings > API Key.');

request.description: Returns {"message":"pong"}. The fastest way to confirm the token and base URL are right.
perPage is capped at 40. Pagination lives under meta.pagination, not meta.
Returns a bare object, NOT wrapped in `data`. List endpoints wrap; single-resource ones do not.
Counts of web apps, databases, cron jobs and supervisor tasks.

Caps at 20 per page here, unlike the global 40.

Responses include pullKey1/pullKey2 — Git deploy keys. Treat them as secrets.
`user` is a system user ID — omit it and the app lands under the default runcloud account.
dbUser/dbPassword/dbName/dbPrefix are auto-generated when omitted.
Also lists linked databases.

Every field is documented as optional, but RunCloud does not say whether omitted fields are preserved or reset.

Safest approach: GET /settings first and send back the full set with your changes applied. disableFunctions is a security control — losing it silently re-enables exec/shell_exec.
Applies immediately to the live site. No staging step, no rollback.
type: primary | alias | redirect. Configures neither DNS nor HTTPS.
Undocumented response shape. With advanced SSL enabled it returns {data:[{id,name,ssl}]} — one entry per domain, not a single certificate.
Returns {advancedSSL: bool, autoSSL: bool}.

Use environment=staging while testing. Live issuance is rate-limited per domain per week and repeated failures lock a domain out for days.

HSTS is close to irreversible — browsers cache it long after you turn it off.
Do not save a real private key into this collection — Postman syncs collections to the cloud by default.

body.raw:
{
  "provider": "custom",
  "certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\\n...",
  "privateKey": "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\\n...",
  "enableHttp": true,
  "enableHsts": false
}

request.description: There is no rename endpoint in v3. The only correction is delete and recreate.
`id` is the database USER id, and it is a single integer despite the plural endpoint name.
Path is lowercase `databaseusers`, no separator.
The response does NOT echo the password back. Capture it now or lose it.
Note there is NO /password suffix here, unlike the system-user equivalent. Returns an empty object.
deploymentKey is the PUBLIC SSH key — safe to paste into GitHub deploy keys.
This password is SSH and SFTP access to the server.
Note the /password suffix here — the database-user equivalent has none.
Replaces any existing key. Every repo registered against the old one stops deploying.
Returns the gitId the other requests need. 403 here usually means the API key lacks the Git scope — check Workspace > Settings > API Key.
`repository` is the path (acme/website), not a URL. Writes into the live app root.

PATCH here EDITS the script. PUT on this same URL RUNS it. The verb is the only difference — see the next request.

Replaces the script outright rather than appending.

PUT runs the script. PATCH on this identical URL rewrites it instead. Easy to get backwards.

Runs asynchronously and returns nothing useful — check the activity log in the dashboard.

Keyed object, not a list, and not paginated.

The `realName` field is the systemd unit and is what the control request needs — NGiNX is nginx-rc, MariaDB is mysql.

action: start | stop | restart | reload. Prefer reload — it does not drop connections.

Use realName from the list request, never the map key.
Schedule comes back as one `time` string; `enabled` is 1/0, not a boolean.
Creation takes five separate fields even though responses return one string. Shorthand like @daily is not accepted.
This FLIPS the current state rather than setting it. Read the job first or you will do the opposite of what you intended.
Keyed by job label. FATAL means the process died and Supervisor gave up — usually a bad command or a permissions problem.
numprocs copies run in parallel, each holding memory for the life of the process. Check /supervisors/status afterwards — a bad command surfaces there, not here.

item.name: 99 · Destructive

request.description: Returns the deleted object.
Removing the primary domain effectively takes the site offline.
HTTPS stops working. If HSTS was enabled, visitors may be unable to reach the site at all until it expires in their browser.

A DELETE that requires a JSON body — easy to miss.

deleteUser=true also removes associated users, which may serve OTHER databases.
Web apps live in the user's home directory. Deleting a user that owns web apps destroys those sites and their files. RunCloud gives no warning — check the web app list first.
The deployment script goes with it and is not recoverable. Copy it first if you may want it.
Scheduled work stops silently. To pause instead, use the toggle request.
If it is a queue worker, jobs pile up in the queue rather than erroring.

item.description:
Every request here changes or destroys something and none of them ask twice. Check the variable values before hitting Send.

DELETE /servers/{id} exists in the API but is deliberately not included.
